_note: The example sentence in French, with the English headword rendered in French too.
Seven quotations stay English because they ARE the specimen - the ambiguity of
'Visiting relatives can be tiring', the redundancy of 'It is what it is', the bad
grammar of 'Between you and I'. Those exist in English and nowhere else, so a
translation of them shows the reader nothing. Reported speech is translated.
French borrowed a great many of these words outright, so five are unchanged and
named in english_ok. Several more were reworded to the ordinary French term
instead - ersatz to succedane, canaille to racaille, rodomontade to fanfaronnade,
interstice to joint, involution to complication - because there the French has a
plainer word and the borrowing is the rarer one.
